quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 19

questions.question: Why must you use extra caution when driving near a pedestrian with a white cane?

options.text: The person is deaf.
The person is a police officer.
The person is blind.
The person has poor balance.

questions.correctAnswerText: The person is blind.
questions.explanation: A white cane or guide dog means the pedestrian is blind. Slow down, give them the right-of-way, and be ready to stop to keep them safe.

questions.question: What does a red circle with a slash through it on a sign mean?

options.text: Come to a complete stop.
An action is forbidden.
Some drivers must yield to others.
Drive under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: An action is forbidden.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a slash means no. It tells you that an action is not allowed. These signs are white with red and black markings.

questions.question: Which of the following increases crash risk for distracted drivers?

options.text: CD player
Radio
Cell phone
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above
questions.explanation: Using a cell phone, radio, or CD player takes your attention away from driving and increases crash risk. This includes hands-free phones.

questions.question: Can you cross a double solid yellow centerline to pass another vehicle?

options.text: Yes.
No.
Yes, if there is no oncoming traffic.
Yes, if the vehicle ahead is driving under the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: No.
questions.explanation: Double solid yellow lines mean no passing. You cannot cross them to pass another car. You can only cross them when turning into a driveway or business entrance.

questions.question: When can you pass another vehicle?

options.text: On a hill or curve because oncoming traffic is unlikely.
By driving on the shoulder of the highway.
If your lane has a solid yellow line and the passing lane is clear.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: None of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not pass on hills or curves because you cannot see oncoming traffic. Do not pass by using the shoulder. Do not pass over a solid yellow line. All of these are unsafe and illegal.

questions.question: You must stop at an intersection when you see a:

options.text: Flashing red light.
Steady yellow light.
Yellow arrow.
Flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and then proceed when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: What limits your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory?

options.text: Only a blood alcohol level above the legal limit can
Alcohol does not
Even a small amount of alcohol can
Only a blood alcohol level above 0.05 percent can

questions.correctAnswerText: Even a small amount of alcohol can
questions.explanation: Even one drink affects your concentration, perception, judgment, and memory. Any amount of alcohol reduces your driving ability. Never drink and drive.

questions.question: What should you do when backing up?

options.text: Use only your mirrors.
Flash your lights.
Open your door to check if it is safe.
Turn your head and look through the rear window.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: Always check behind your vehicle before backing. Turn your head to see through the rear window. Children and small objects are hard to see in mirrors. Do not rely only on mirrors or sensors.

questions.question: When turning onto a street with multiple lanes in your direction, which lane should you turn into?

options.text: The lane closest to your previous lane.
The lane marked with an arrow.
The middle lane.
Any lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lane closest to your previous lane.
questions.explanation: Turn into the lane closest to where you came from. Do not change lanes while turning.

questions.question: When passing on a two-lane road with traffic going both ways, when should you return to your lane?

options.text: When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
When you plan to turn left.
Right away.
You can stay in either lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: When there is enough room between you and the vehicle you passed.
questions.explanation: Return to the right side of the road when you have enough space between you and the car you passed. Make sure it is safe before moving back.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Slow down when the road is wet.
The road ahead has curves or sharp turns.
There will be more traffic ahead.
There is a steep hill ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is slippery when wet. When driving on wet pavement, you should slow down, avoid sudden braking or turns, and stay farther away from other vehicles.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When driving through an intersection.
When passing a bicycle rider.
When a child is about to run into the street.
When parallel parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: When a child is about to run into the street.
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn others when they may not see you. For example, honk if a child is about to run into the street in front of your vehicle.

questions.question: What should you do when you see or hear an emergency vehicle?

options.text: Stop right away and let the vehicle pass.
Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
Drive slowly and let the vehicle pass.
Keep driving slowly on the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road as safely as you can and stop.
questions.explanation: When an emergency vehicle is coming with its lights and/or siren on, move as far to the right as you safely can and stop. Do not stop in an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
The shoulder is low.
No parking at any time.
This lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This sign tells drivers to stay in the right lane to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: What factors affect how alcohol impacts your body?

options.text: How much food is in your stomach.
Your body weight.
How much time passes between drinks.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Your blood alcohol level depends on how much you drink, how much time passes between drinks, and your weight. Eating food can slow alcohol absorption, but it cannot prevent getting drunk if you drink too much.

questions.question: Which statement about drowsy drivers is true?

options.text: Black coffee will keep them awake.
They may drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
Opening a window and loud radio will keep them alert.
Only older drivers get drowsy.

questions.correctAnswerText: They may drive so poorly that they seem drunk.
questions.explanation: Drowsy drivers can drive so poorly that they look like drunk drivers. Coffee, open windows, and loud radio are not enough to help a drowsy driver stay alert.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is a sharp turn ahead—slow down.
There is a work crew ahead.
There is a side road ahead.
There is a playground ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is a sharp turn ahead—slow down.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are usually yellow with black markings. This sign warns you to slow down because there is a sharp turn coming.

questions.question: You are in the right lane on a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check your mirrors and look over your shoulder to make sure the lane is clear. Always use your signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a flashing red traffic light?

options.text: Drive through if no other cars are coming.
Keep driving—you have the right-of-way.
Stop only if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Flashing red lights appear at dangerous intersections. Treat them the same way you treat stop signs.

questions.question: If you need to stop quickly and your car does not have anti-lock brakes, what should you do?

options.text: Press the brake pedal down hard.
Pump the brakes firmly.
Tap the brakes lightly.
Release the brake pedal.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brakes firmly.
questions.explanation: Pumping the brakes is the best way to stop quickly in an emergency. Your car will stop faster and you can still steer.

questions.question: Which recommendation does NOT help with safe night driving?

options.text: Keep your windshield clean.
Know that tinted windows make it harder to see in the dark.
Carry a flashlight in your vehicle.
Look at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look at the headlights of oncoming vehicles.
questions.explanation: If you look at oncoming headlights, your pupils shrink. After the car passes, your pupils need time to adjust to the darker light. During this time, you cannot see well.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: U-turns are not allowed.
U-turns are allowed.
Curvy road ahead.
Sharp left turn ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: U-turns are not allowed.
questions.explanation: A red circle with a red line through it means something is not allowed. This sign means you cannot make a U-turn.

questions.question: What should you do if traffic lights are out due to a power outage?

options.text: Park your vehicle off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to show other drivers what you will do.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat the intersection like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is broken, treat it like a four-way stop. Let other drivers go first if needed, then go through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: What happens as alcohol builds up in your blood?

options.text: Your reactions slow down.
You feel less confident.
Your body breaks it down faster.
You make fewer driving mistakes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your reactions slow down.
questions.explanation: As alcohol builds up in your body, your reactions get slower. You feel more confident but make more mistakes.

questions.question: When should you drive below the posted speed limit?

options.text: When anything makes driving conditions not perfect.
When you see a police car.
When entering a highway with other cars.
When you are on a four-lane road.

questions.correctAnswerText: When anything makes driving conditions not perfect.
questions.explanation: Drive below the speed limit when the road is wet, when you cannot see well, or when anything else is not perfect. You can get a ticket for driving too fast for conditions, even if you are at the speed limit.
